headline: A developer released an open-source tool that lets AI models design LEGO models of more than 2,000 pieces, though none has been built.
score_reason: Hobby project released 2 Oct 2026, before the window; designs unbuilt.
importance_line: It matters to hobbyists and AI developers, but the designs are untested in real bricks and the tool does not check whether a model stays standing.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that developer Carlos Antelo released LDraw Nova on Friday 2 Oct 2026, an open-source tool in which AI models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra write programs that produce LEGO design files, including a 2,175-piece Sakura Garden. None of the designs has been built from real bricks, and the tool does not yet model physics, so stability is not checked.
